I need to answer this question about the repository at /bench/repo: "What background workers/runners does the server actually START, and what drives each one's scheduling? Note explicitly if any scheduling infrastructure present in the codebase is NOT used by the server."

Please investigate:
1. Find the server's main entry point / bootstrap code (e.g. server startup file, app initialization).
2. Find all places where background workers, jobs, cron tasks, queues, schedulers, intervals (setInterval/setTimeout loops), or similar recurring/async runners are STARTED as part of server startup (not just defined).
3. For each one that is actually started, identify what triggers/schedules it (e.g. cron expression, fixed interval, event-driven queue consumer, webhook, etc.) and cite the file path and line number where it's started and where the schedule/trigger is configured.
4. Look for any scheduling infrastructure (e.g. a generic job scheduler class, cron library setup, queue library setup, agenda/bull/bee-queue setup, a "jobs" or "scheduler" directory) that exists in the codebase but is NOT actually wired up / started / used by the running server (e.g. defined but never imported/called, or only used in tests, or leftover/deprecated code).

This is likely a monorepo — check for multiple services/packages (e.g. apps/, packages/, server/, api/, worker/ directories). Focus specifically on what the SERVER process starts, not what CLI tools or standalone scripts might start.

Report back with specific file paths and line numbers for every finding. Be thorough - check package.json scripts, main/index files, any "worker.ts", "scheduler.ts", "cron.ts", "jobs.ts" files, and any place that imports node-cron, bull, bullmq, agenda, node-schedule, etc.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

27	)

29	const shutdownTimeout = 10 * time.Second
30	
31	type Server struct {
32		Secret  string
33		Profile *profile.Profile
34		Store   *store.Store
35	
36		echoServer *echo.Echo
37		httpServer *http.Server
38		sseHub     *apiv1.SSEHub
39	
40		backgroundRunnerCancels []context.CancelFunc
41		backgroundRunnerWG      sync.WaitGroup
42	}
43	
44	func NewServer(ctx context.Context, profile *profile.Profile, store *store.Store) (*Server, error) {
45		s := &Server{
46			Store:   store,
47			Profile: profile,
48		}
49	
50		echoServer := echo.New()
51		echoServer.Use(middleware.Recover())
52		echoServer.Use(newCORSMiddleware(profile))
53		s.echoServer = echoServer
54	
55		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.getOrUpsertInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
56		if err != nil {
57			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
58		}
59	
60		secret := "usememos"
61		if !profile.Demo {
62			secret = instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey
63		}
64		s.Secret = secret
65	
66		// Register healthz endpoint.
67		echoServer.GET("/healthz", func(c *echo.Context) error {
68			return c.String(http.StatusOK, "Service ready.")
69		})
70	
71		// Serve frontend static files.
72		frontend.NewFrontendService(profile, store).Serve(ctx, echoServer)
73	
74		rootGroup := echoServer.Group("")
75	
76		apiV1Service := apiv1.NewAPIV1Service(s.Secret, profile, store)
77		s.sseHub = apiV1Service.SSEHub
78	
79		// Register HTTP file server routes BEFORE gRPC-Gateway to ensure proper range request handling for Safari.
80		// This uses native HTTP serving (http.ServeContent) instead of gRPC for video/audio files.
81		fileServerService := fileserver.NewFileServerService(s.Profile, s.Store, s.Secret)
82		fileServerService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)
83	
84		// Create and register RSS routes (needs markdown service from apiV1Service).
85		rss.NewRSSService(s.Profile, s.Store, apiV1Service.MarkdownService).RegisterRoutes(rootGroup)
86	
87		// Register gRPC gateway as api v1 (includes SSE endpoint on CORS-enabled group).
88		if err := apiV1Service.RegisterGateway(ctx, echoServer); err != nil {
89			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to register gRPC gateway")
90		}
91	
92		mcpService, err := mcp.NewMCPService(profile, echoServer)
93		if err != nil {
94			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to create MCP service")
95		}
96		mcpService.RegisterRoutes(echoServer)
97	
98		return s, nil
99	}
100	
101	func (s *Server) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
102		var address, network string
103		if len(s.Profile.UNIXSock) == 0 {
104			address = fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", s.Profile.Addr, s.Profile.Port)
105			network = "tcp"
106		} else {
107			address = s.Profile.UNIXSock
108			network = "unix"
109		}
110		listener, err := net.Listen(network, address)
111		if err != nil {
112			return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to listen")
113		}
114	
115		if network == "unix" {
116			if err := os.Chmod(address, 0660); err != nil {
117				_ = listener.Close()
118				return errors.Wrap(err, "failed to chmod socket")
119			}
120		}
121	
122		// Start Echo server directly (no cmux needed - all traffic is HTTP).
123		s.httpServer = &http.Server{Handler: s.echoServer}
124		go func() {
125			if err := s.httpServer.Serve(listener); err != nil && err != http.ErrServerClosed {
126				slog.Error("failed to start echo server", "error", err)
127			}
128		}()
129		s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)
130	
131		return nil
132	}
133	
134	func (s *Server) Shutdown(ctx context.Context) {
135		ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, shutdownTimeout)
136		defer cancel()
137	
138		slog.Info("server shutting down")
139	
140		s.stopBackgroundRunners()
141		s.closeLongLivedConnections()
142		s.shutdownHTTPServer(ctx)
143		s.waitBackgroundRunners(ctx)
144	
145		// Close database connection.
146		if err := s.Store.Close(); err != nil {
147			slog.Error("failed to close database", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
148		}
149	
150		slog.Info("memos stopped properly")
151	}
152	
153	func (s *Server) startBackgroundRunners(ctx context.Context) {
154		// Create a separate context for each background runner
155		// This allows us to control cancellation for each runner independently
156		s3Context, s3Cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
157	
158		// Store the cancel function so we can properly shut down runners
159		s.backgroundRunnerCancels = append(s.backgroundRunnerCancels, s3Cancel)
160	
161		// Create and start S3 presign runner
162		s3presignRunner := s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)
163		s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)
164	
165		// Start continuous S3 presign runner
166		s.backgroundRunnerWG.Add(1)
167		go func() {
168			defer s.backgroundRunnerWG.Done()
169			s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context)
170			slog.Info("s3presign runner stopped")
171		}()
172	
173		slog.Info("background runners started")
174	}
175	
176	func (s *Server) stopBackgroundRunners() {
177		for _, cancelFunc := range s.backgroundRunnerCancels {
178			if cancelFunc != nil {
179				cancelFunc()
180			}
181		}
182	}
183	
184	func (s *Server) waitBackgroundRunners(ctx context.Context) {
185		done := make(chan struct{})
186		go func() {
187			s.backgroundRunnerWG.Wait()
188			close(done)
189		}()
190	
191		select {
192		case <-done:
193		case <-ctx.Done():
194			select {
195			case <-done:
196				return
197			default:
198			}
199			slog.Error("failed to stop background runners", slog.String("error", ctx.Err().Error()))
200		}
201	}
202	
203	func (s *Server) closeLongLivedConnections() {
204		// Long-lived SSE requests do not finish on their own during http.Server.Shutdown.
205		if s.sseHub != nil {
206			s.sseHub.Close()
207		}
208	}
209	
210	func (s *Server) shutdownHTTPServer(ctx context.Context) {
211		if s.httpServer == nil {
212			return
213		}
214		if err := s.httpServer.Shutdown(ctx); err != nil {
215			slog.Error("failed to shutdown server", slog.String("error", err.Error()))
216			if closeErr := s.httpServer.Close(); closeErr != nil && closeErr != http.ErrServerClosed {
217				slog.Error("failed to close server", slog.String("error", closeErr.Error()))
218			}
219		}
220	}
221	
222	func (s *Server) getOrUpsertInstanceBasicSetting(ctx context.Context) (*storepb.InstanceBasicSetting, error) {
223		instanceBasicSetting, err := s.Store.GetInstanceBasicSetting(ctx)
224		if err != nil {
225			return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to get instance basic setting")
226		}
227		modified := false
228		if instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey == "" {
229			instanceBasicSetting.SecretKey = uuid.NewString()
230			modified = true
231		}
232		if modified {
233			instanceSetting, err := s.Store.UpsertInstanceSetting(ctx, &storepb.InstanceSetting{
234				Key:   storepb.InstanceSettingKey_BASIC,
235				Value: &storepb.InstanceSetting_BasicSetting{BasicSetting: instanceBasicSetting},
236			})
237			if err != nil {
238				return nil, errors.Wrap(err, "failed to upsert instance setting")
239			}
240			instanceBasicSetting = instanceSetting.GetBasicSetting()
241		}
242		return instanceBasicSetting, nil
243	}

36

1	# Scheduler Plugin
2	
3	A production-ready, GitHub Actions-inspired cron job scheduler for Go.
4	
5	## Features
6	
7	- **Standard Cron Syntax**: Supports both 5-field and 6-field (with seconds) cron expressions
8	- **Timezone-Aware**: Explicit timezone handling to avoid DST surprises
9	- **Middleware Pattern**: Composable job wrappers for logging, metrics, panic recovery, timeouts
10	- **Graceful Shutdown**: Jobs complete cleanly or cancel when context expires
11	- **Zero Dependencies**: Core functionality uses only the standard library
12	- **Type-Safe**: Strong typing with clear error messages
13	- **Well-Tested**: Comprehensive test coverage
14	
15	## Installation
16	
17	This package is included with Memos. No separate installation required.
18	
19	## Quick Start
20	
21	```go
22	package main
23	
24	import (
25	    "context"
26	    "fmt"
27	    "github.com/usememos/memos/internal/scheduler"
28	)
29	
30	func main() {
31	    s := scheduler.New()
32	
33	    s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
34	        Name:     "daily-cleanup",
35	        Schedule: "0 2 * * *", // 2 AM daily
36	        Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
37	            fmt.Println("Running cleanup...")
38	            return nil
39	        },
40	    })
41	
42	    s.Start()
43	    defer s.Stop(context.Background())
44	
45	    // Keep running...
46	    select {}
47	}
48	```
49	
50	## Cron Expression Format
51	
52	### 5-Field Format (Standard)
53	```
54	┌───────────── minute (0 - 59)
55	│ ┌───────────── hour (0 - 23)
56	│ │ ┌───────────── day of month (1 - 31)
57	│ │ │ ┌───────────── month (1 - 12)
58	│ │ │ │ ┌───────────── day of week (0 - 7) (Sunday = 0 or 7)
59	│ │ │ │ │
60	* * * * *
61	```
62	
63	### 6-Field Format (With Seconds)
64	```
65	┌───────────── second (0 - 59)
66	│ ┌───────────── minute (0 - 59)
67	│ │ ┌───────────── hour (0 - 23)
68	│ │ │ ┌───────────── day of month (1 - 31)
69	│ │ │ │ ┌───────────── month (1 - 12)
70	│ │ │ │ │ ┌───────────── day of week (0 - 7)
71	│ │ │ │ │ │
72	* * * * * *
73	```
74	
75	### Special Characters
76	
77	- `*` - Any value (every minute, every hour, etc.)
78	- `,` - List of values: `1,15,30` (1st, 15th, and 30th)
79	- `-` - Range: `9-17` (9 AM through 5 PM)
80	- `/` - Step: `*/15` (every 15 units)
81	
82	### Common Examples
83	
84	| Schedule | Description |
85	|----------|-------------|
86	| `* * * * *` | Every minute |
87	| `0 * * * *` | Every hour |
88	| `0 0 * * *` | Daily at midnight |
89	| `0 9 * * 1-5` | Weekdays at 9 AM |
90	| `*/15 * * * *` | Every 15 minutes |
91	| `0 0 1 * *` | First day of every month |
92	| `0 0 * * 0` | Every Sunday at midnight |
93	| `30 14 * * *` | Every day at 2:30 PM |
94	
95	## Timezone Support
96	
97	```go
98	// Global timezone for all jobs
99	s := scheduler.New(
100	    scheduler.WithTimezone("America/New_York"),
101	)
102	
103	// Per-job timezone (overrides global)
104	s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
105	    Name:     "tokyo-report",
106	    Schedule: "0 9 * * *", // 9 AM Tokyo time
107	    Timezone: "Asia/Tokyo",
108	    Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
109	        // Runs at 9 AM in Tokyo
110	        return nil
111	    },
112	})
113	```
114	
115	**Important**: Always use IANA timezone names (`America/New_York`, not `EST`).
116	
117	## Middleware
118	
119	Middleware wraps job handlers to add cross-cutting behavior. Multiple middleware can be chained together.
120	
121	### Built-in Middleware
122	
123	#### Recovery (Panic Handling)
124	
125	```go
126	s := scheduler.New(
127	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
128	        scheduler.Recovery(func(jobName string, r interface{}) {
129	            log.Printf("Job %s panicked: %v", jobName, r)
130	        }),
131	    ),
132	)
133	```
134	
135	#### Logging
136	
137	```go
138	type Logger interface {
139	    Info(msg string, args ...interface{})
140	    Error(msg string, args ...interface{})
141	}
142	
143	s := scheduler.New(
144	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
145	        scheduler.Logging(myLogger),
146	    ),
147	)
148	```
149	
150	#### Timeout
151	
152	```go
153	s := scheduler.New(
154	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
155	        scheduler.Timeout(5 * time.Minute),
156	    ),
157	)
158	```
159	
160	### Combining Middleware
161	
162	```go
163	s := scheduler.New(
164	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
165	        scheduler.Recovery(panicHandler),
166	        scheduler.Logging(logger),
167	        scheduler.Timeout(10 * time.Minute),
168	    ),
169	)
170	```
171	
172	**Order matters**: Middleware are applied left-to-right. In the example above:
173	1. Recovery (outermost) catches panics from everything
174	2. Logging logs the execution
175	3. Timeout (innermost) wraps the actual handler
176	
177	### Custom Middleware
178	
179	```go
180	func Metrics(recorder MetricsRecorder) scheduler.Middleware {
181	    return func(next scheduler.JobHandler) scheduler.JobHandler {
182	        return func(ctx context.Context) error {
183	            start := time.Now()
184	            err := next(ctx)
185	            duration := time.Since(start)
186	
187	            jobName := scheduler.GetJobName(ctx)
188	            recorder.Record(jobName, duration, err)
189	
190	            return err
191	        }
192	    }
193	}
194	```
195	
196	## Graceful Shutdown
197	
198	Always use `Stop()` with a context to allow jobs to finish cleanly:
199	
200	```go
201	// Give jobs up to 30 seconds to complete
202	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
203	defer cancel()
204	
205	if err := s.Stop(ctx); err != nil {
206	    log.Printf("Shutdown error: %v", err)
207	}
208	```
209	
210	Jobs should respect context cancellation:
211	
212	```go
213	Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
214	    for i := 0; i < 100; i++ {
215	        select {
216	        case <-ctx.Done():
217	            return ctx.Err() // Canceled
218	        default:
219	            // Do work
220	        }
221	    }
222	    return nil
223	}
224	```
225	
226	## Best Practices
227	
228	### 1. Always Name Your Jobs
229	
230	Names are used for logging, metrics, and debugging:
231	
232	```go
233	Name: "user-cleanup-job" // Good
234	Name: "job1"             // Bad
235	```
236	
237	### 2. Add Descriptions and Tags
238	
239	```go
240	s.Register(&scheduler.Job{
241	    Name:        "stale-session-cleanup",
242	    Description: "Removes user sessions older than 30 days",
243	    Tags:        []string{"maintenance", "security"},
244	    Schedule:    "0 3 * * *",
245	    Handler:     cleanupSessions,
246	})
247	```
248	
249	### 3. Use Appropriate Middleware
250	
251	Always include Recovery and Logging in production:
252	
253	```go
254	scheduler.New(
255	    scheduler.WithMiddleware(
256	        scheduler.Recovery(logPanic),
257	        scheduler.Logging(logger),
258	    ),
259	)
260	```
261	
262	### 4. Avoid Scheduling Exactly on the Hour
263	
264	Many systems schedule jobs at `:00`, causing load spikes. Stagger your jobs:
265	
266	```go
267	"5 2 * * *"  // 2:05 AM (good)
268	"0 2 * * *"  // 2:00 AM (often overloaded)
269	```
270	
271	### 5. Make Jobs Idempotent
272	
273	Jobs may run multiple times (crash recovery, etc.). Design them to be safely re-runnable:
274	
275	```go
276	Handler: func(ctx context.Context) error {
277	    // Use unique constraint or check-before-insert
278	    db.Exec("INSERT IGNORE INTO processed_items ...")
279	    return nil
280	}
281	```
282	
283	### 6. Handle Timezones Explicitly
284	
285	Always specify timezone for business-hour jobs:
286	
287	```go
288	Timezone: "America/New_York" // Good
289	// Timezone: ""              // Bad (defaults to UTC)
290	```
291	
292	### 7. Test Your Cron Expressions
293	
294	Use a cron expression calculator before deploying:
295	- [crontab.guru](https://crontab.guru/)
296	- Write unit tests with the parser
297	
298	## Testing Jobs
299	
300	Test job handlers independently of the scheduler:
301	
302	```go
303	func TestCleanupJob(t *testing.T) {
304	    ctx := context.Background()
305	
306	    err := cleanupHandler(ctx)
307	    if err != nil {
308	        t.Fatalf("cleanup failed: %v", err)
309	    }
310	
311	    // Verify cleanup occurred
312	}
313	```
314	
315	Test schedule parsing:
316	
317	```go
318	func TestScheduleParsing(t *testing.T) {
319	    job := &scheduler.Job{
320	        Name:     "test",
321	        Schedule: "0 2 * * *",
322	        Handler:  func(ctx context.Context) error { return nil },
323	    }
324	
325	    if err := job.Validate(); err != nil {
326	        t.Fatalf("invalid job: %v", err)
327	    }
328	}
329	```
330	
331	## Comparison to Other Solutions
332	
333	| Feature | scheduler | robfig/cron | github.com/go-co-op/gocron |
334	|---------|-----------|-------------|----------------------------|
335	| Standard cron syntax | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
336	| Seconds support | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
337	| Timezone support | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
338	| Middleware pattern | ✅ | ⚠️ (basic) | ❌ |
339	| Graceful shutdown | ✅ | ⚠️ (basic) | ✅ |
340	| Zero dependencies | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ |
341	| Job metadata | ✅ | ❌ | ⚠️ (limited) |
342	
343	## API Reference
344	
345	See [example_test.go](./example_test.go) for comprehensive examples.
346	
347	### Core Types
348	
349	- `Scheduler` - Manages scheduled jobs
350	- `Job` - Job definition with schedule and handler
351	- `Middleware` - Function that wraps job handlers
352	
353	### Functions
354	
355	- `New(opts ...Option) *Scheduler` - Create new scheduler
356	- `WithTimezone(tz string) Option` - Set default timezone
357	- `WithMiddleware(mw ...Middleware) Option` - Add middleware
358	
359	### Methods
360	
361	- `Register(job *Job) error` - Add job to scheduler
362	- `Start() error` - Begin executing jobs
363	- `Stop(ctx context.Context) error` - Graceful shutdown
364	
365	## License
366	
367	This package is part of the Memos project and shares its license.

# Background Workers/Runners Started by the Memos Server

This is a Go monorepo (the `usememos/memos` note-taking app), with a single server binary (`cmd/memos`) and a frontend SPA in `web/` (no runtime relevance). Everything below is about the Go server process.

## Entry point / bootstrap

- `/bench/repo/cmd/memos/main.go` — cobra `rootCmd.Run` (lines 36–107) is the bootstrap: creates the DB driver, calls `store.New(...)` (line 64), runs migrations, then `server.NewServer(...)` (line 76) and `s.Start(ctx)` (line 89).
- `/bench/repo/server/server.go` — `Server.Start` (line 101) starts the HTTP listener and, at line 129, calls `s.startBackgroundRunners(ctx)` (defined lines 153–174). This is the actual "what gets started" chokepoint for scheduled/recurring workers.

## Workers actually started

### 1. S3 presign runner — the only registered "background runner"
- Started at `/bench/repo/server/server.go:161-171`, inside `startBackgroundRunners`:
  - `s3presignRunner := s3presign.NewRunner(s.Store)` (line 162)
  - `s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)` — runs immediately once at startup (line 163)
  - `go func() { s3presignRunner.Run(s3Context) }()` — launched as a goroutine, tracked via `backgroundRunnerWG`/`backgroundRunnerCancels` for graceful shutdown (lines 166-171)
- Scheduling mechanism: a plain `time.NewTicker` fixed interval loop, **not** cron. Defined in `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go`:
  - `const runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12` (line 27, comment: "Schedule runner every 12 hours")
  - `Run(ctx)` (lines 29-41) does `ticker := time.NewTicker(runnerInterval)` and calls `r.RunOnce(ctx)` on every tick until `ctx.Done()`.
  - Purpose: re-presigns S3 object URLs for attachments whose presigned URL is within 4 days of its 5-day expiry (see `CheckAndPresign`, lines 47-131).

This is the **only** worker the server registers as a long-running/recurring background loop.

### 2. Store-level cache cleanup loops (started before the HTTP server, but still part of server startup)
- `/bench/repo/store/store.go:37-59` (`store.New`) creates three in-memory caches: `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache` (lines 51-53), each via `cache.New(cacheConfig)` with `CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute` (line 42).
- `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go:75-84` (`cache.New`) spawns a goroutine per cache: `go c.cleanupLoop()` (line 82).
- Scheduling mechanism: `cleanupLoop` (lines 199-215) uses `time.NewTicker(c.config.CleanupInterval)` — a fixed 5-minute interval ticker, purely to evict expired TTL entries.
- `store.New(...)` is invoked from `/bench/repo/cmd/memos/main.go:64`, i.e. before `server.NewServer`/`s.Start`, so these three ticker-driven goroutines are indeed started as part of normal server bootstrap. Shutdown is via `Store.Close()` (`/bench/repo/store/store.go:72-79`), which calls `.Close()` on each cache to stop its goroutine, invoked from `Server.Shutdown` (`server.go:146`).

### 3. Fixed-size async worker pools (event-driven, not time-scheduled)
These are goroutine pools consuming from buffered channels, started via Go `init()` functions the moment the owning package is imported/linked into the binary (which happens because `server`/`cmd/memos` import them transitively) — not gated behind any explicit "start" call, and not schedule-driven at all, but they are recurring background consumers so worth listing:
- `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go:39-55` — `asyncPostQueue := make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` (line 39); `init()` (lines 42-55) launches 4 goroutines that range over the channel and call `Post(payload)`. Trigger: whenever application code enqueues a webhook dispatch (event-driven consumer, not cron/interval).
- `/bench/repo/internal/email/email.go:14-36` — `asyncEmailQueue := make(chan asyncEmailRequest, 128)` (line 14); `init()` (lines 16-36) launches 2 goroutines that range over the channel and call `Send(...)`. Trigger: application code enqueuing an email send (event-driven).
- `/bench/repo/server/auth/authenticator.go:178-184` (`recordPATUsage`) — a one-off `go func(){...}()` per call to asynchronously update PAT last-used time; not a persistent worker/loop, just fire-and-forget per request.

### Not a background worker (event-driven, per-connection only)
- `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go:64` — `heartbeat := time.NewTicker(sseHeartbeatInterval)` (30s, defined line 18) is created **per SSE client connection** inside `handleSSE`, not at server startup. It's request-scoped, not a global scheduled runner.

### Not a recurring worker (runs synchronously, once, on demand)
- `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go` — defines a `Runner` type with only `RunOnce(ctx)` (lines 27-72); there is no `Run`/loop/ticker in this package at all. Grepping usages shows it is **never instantiated via `NewRunner`/`RunOnce` as a background job** — instead only the standalone helper function `RebuildMemoPayload` (line 74) is called synchronously and inline from request handlers in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` and `:447` (on memo create/update). So despite living under `server/runner/`, this "runner" is not started as a background process by the server; it's dead code as a runner and only its helper function is reused synchronously.

## Scheduling infrastructure present but NOT used by the server

**`/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/`** — a full, self-contained "GitHub Actions–inspired cron job scheduler" package with real cron-expression parsing (5- and 6-field), timezone support, middleware (Recovery/Logging/Timeout), and graceful shutdown:
- `scheduler.go` (`Scheduler`, `New`, `Register`, `Start`, `Stop` — types/funcs listed at lines 12, 54, etc.)
- `job.go` (`Job`, `JobHandler`)
- `parser.go` (cron expression parser, `Schedule` struct)
- `middleware.go` (`Recovery`, `Logging`, `Timeout` middleware)
- `doc.go` explicitly documents usage: `s := scheduler.New(); s.Register(&scheduler.Job{Schedule: "0 2 * * *", ...}); s.Start()`
- `README.md` markets it as production-ready with a comparison table vs. `robfig/cron` / `gocron`.

**It is never imported anywhere outside its own package.** I confirmed via `grep -rln "usememos/memos/internal/scheduler"` across the whole repo that the only files importing it are its own test files (`internal/scheduler/example_test.go`, `internal/scheduler/integration_test.go`) — i.e. it demonstrates and tests itself but is not wired into `cmd/memos/main.go`, `server/server.go`, or any router/service. No `scheduler.New(`/`.Register(`/`.Start(` call exists anywhere in `/bench/repo/server`, `/bench/repo/cmd`, or `/bench/repo/store`.

**Conclusion: `internal/scheduler` is fully-built, cron-capable scheduling infrastructure that the running server does NOT start or use at all** — it's effectively unused/leftover (or speculative/library-in-waiting) code, exercised only by its own test suite.

## Summary table

| Runner | Started at | Trigger/schedule | Wired into server? |
|---|---|---|---|
| S3 presign runner | `server/server.go:161-171` | `time.Ticker`, fixed 12h (`server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27,30`) | Yes — only registered `backgroundRunner` |
| Cache cleanup ×3 (instance setting/user/user setting) | `store/store.go:51-53` via `cache.New` → `store/cache/cache.go:82` | `time.Ticker`, fixed 5min (`store/cache/cache.go:44`) | Yes — started during `store.New()` in `cmd/memos/main.go:64`, before `server.NewServer` |
| Webhook async dispatch pool (4 goroutines) | `internal/webhook/webhook.go:42-55` (package `init()`) | Event-driven, channel consumer (buffered chan, cap 128) | Yes — implicit at process load, no cron |
| Email async send pool (2 goroutines) | `internal/email/email.go:16-36` (package `init()`) | Event-driven, channel consumer (buffered chan, cap 128) | Yes — implicit at process load, no cron |
| SSE heartbeat ticker | `server/router/api/v1/sse_handler.go:64` | `time.Ticker`, 30s, but per-connection not global | Yes, but scoped to each SSE request, not a startup-time background runner |
| `memopayload.Runner` (Run/loop) | N/A | N/A | **Not started as a runner** — only its `RebuildMemoPayload` helper is called synchronously from `memo_service.go:108,447` |
| `internal/scheduler` (cron scheduler package) | N/A | Cron expressions (fully implemented) | **Never used** — only referenced by its own tests |
